title: Continual Neural Topic Model
task: Learning topic models over successive time steps without forgetting earlier topics
problem: Dynamic topic models need the whole corpus in advance, while online topic models lack long-term memory.
architecture: CoNTM builds on the Dirichlet VAE: each time slice has local topics derived from a continuously updated global topic set (local topics = g(global topics, local offsets)); the global prior carries topic dependencies from the previous step so new data can be learned online without forgetting.
metrics: NPMI coherence with a temporal reference corpus
predictive perplexity on future time slices
key_results: Best average rank on topic quality (1.6) across six datasets with 50 topics; e.g. NYT TQ .173 vs .135 (DETM) and .117 (CFDTM).
On the Tweets dataset its TQ is negative (-.006) while Dynamic BERTopic reaches .096.
strengths: Learns from a data stream without requiring all data up front.
Few extra parameters compared with models that explicitly model each transition.

limitations.text: Needs large amounts of data; may struggle with sparse data or rapidly evolving topics (e.g. social media).
Assumes a fixed number of topics and does not model topic birth or death.
Coherence metrics may not capture semantic shifts over time.
